editorial:
Imagine a world where a greedy guy named Graal wants to steal the throne from his own brother. To do it, he teams up with a crazy scientist who has a secret chemical that turns regular people into killing machines. They pick a poor pilot named Golob to be their first test subject. Suddenly, Golob is no longer a man; he is a mindless robot with super strength who can't be stopped. You get a real sense of dread as you watch these villains try to build an entire army of these monsters to take over the planet Metropolis. It feels like an old-school comic book come to life with a weird, trippy vibe.

You will notice that the special effects are a bit dated, but that actually adds to the charm. The acting is over-the-top, which makes the battle for the planet feel like a wild ride. While the plot is simple, the action keeps you moving. If you love weird 70s sci-fi, you should definitely track this down. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend.
endingExplained: In the end, the heroes fight back to stop Graal's plan. The mindless soldier Golob eventually becomes a liability to his creators. During the final chaos, the evil plans crumble as the people of Metropolis fight for their freedom. The chemical process is stopped, and Graal is defeated before he can turn the whole population into robots. Peace is restored to the planet, and the threat of the humanoid army is finally wiped out for good.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage space movies and campy villains.
